judgements.justification: B's area chair adopted no single outlier's verdict: nDd9's 4 was set aside, and 1UMR's 8 asked for no oral; the oral rests on an off-record novelty judgement.
Neither area chair set the tier by the mean: B's mean (6.5) is below A's (6.67), yet B went higher.
B's scores were not unanimous (nDd9 gave 4), and A's 6, 7, 7 held A at a poster.
No score rose after the rebuttal in either committee; eRj1's final 7 fits its pre-response text.
B's meta-review names the writing and the comparison to past work as 'very substantial concerns', and A's carries its reviewers' requests forward.
A's reviewers misstated the bound as linear in k and nDd9 misread the dimensions, but nothing shows either error moved a score or the tier.
The authors conceded to B that the theory is 'less clear' for the dependent trees of boosting used in the experiments; no B score fell and B's area chair still gave an oral.
All of B's objections, including nDd9's, came in the initial reviews, before the response period.
B's area chair did not cite only scores: it gave its own novelty judgement ('absolutely above the bar'), and B's reviews found more faults than A's.
B's best-informed reviewer, ybbQ (7, six hours), argued for accept, and B's area chair went above, not to, the less-informed mean.
The response moved no score in either committee.
nDd9's outlying 4 lowered B's mean below A's, but B still went higher, so the outlier did not set the tier.
nDd9 did not reply, but the response did not answer nDd9's basis (histogram work still uncited, forest gap conceded), and the 4 did not hold B down.
B had a detractor but went to an oral, so its decision did not stop at a plain accept.
No reviewer or area chair raised audience breadth or venue fit.
The 'absolutely above the bar' quote appears in no public record, but the notes cannot show it misreports a private discussion; the meta-review states the writing and past-work concerns accurately.
Most reviewers in both committees left the response unanswered, and no reviewer in either committee revised a score.

B's Reviewer_1UMR gave an 8 at confidence 2 without checking the math; it is B's only score above 7, and B's area chair drew on its praise for an oral that its checked reviews (4, 7, 7) did not support.
B's reviewers split three accepts to one reject, not evenly.
The notes show the responses addressed different questions, but no conflicting results or accounts between the two committees.
nDd9 and BfeE named uncited related work, but the notes do not show that this work contradicts the 'first coreset for decision trees' claim.
No B reviewer argued for an oral, B's mean is below A's, and B's meta-review calls the writing 'almost ... unpublishable'; nothing in the public record argues for the oral tier.
nDd9 cited missing database work but objected to the writing and coverage gaps, not to the paper's framing or definitions.
Neither committee had an engaged champion: B's only score above 7 came from a two-sentence review with no discussion.
Neither committee held promised revisions too large for camera-ready; B treated the writing as fixable.
B's oral rests on 'absolutely above the bar', a judgement that appears in no public review or comment, used to set a tier that the visible reviews did not support.
Both committees judged the paper as a theory-plus-experiments coreset contribution by the same standards.
nDd9's 4 rests on writing, missing related work and the single-tree-versus-forest gap, which are central, not peripheral.
